sce:cc-care-2025-11-15: Special Condition 8 of Schedule TOU-D, the California Alternate Rates for Energy Discount, carries one benefit that dominates all the others and that this filing does not represent: a 32.5 percent discount taken off the customer's bill before the Public Utilities Commission Reimbursement Fee and any applicable user fees, taxes and late payment charges. What is modeled is the set of per-line-item exemptions the same Special Condition grants, namely the Wildfire Fund Non-Bypassable Charge of $0.00595 per kWh, the Fixed Recovery Charge of $0.00198 per kWh, the Base Services Charge Surcharge of $0.063 per meter per day, and a Base Services Charge Discount of $(0.153) per meter per day. Special Condition 8 also exempts CARE customers from the CARE Surcharge of $0.212 per meter per day; that surcharge is not itemized on any SCE residential rate sheet in this corpus, so there is no base line item for the exemption to cancel and it is absent here. Because the unmodeled percentage applies to the whole bill while the modeled credits are fixed per-kWh and per-meter-per-day line items, a typical CARE household's modeled credits fall well short of the actual benefit. Two further provisions of Special Condition 8 are out of scope rather than missing: the application and eligibility declaration, and the rebilling of periods in which the customer did not qualify, are enrollment and billing-administration procedures rather than rates.
sce:cc-care-2026-03-20: Sheet 1 of Schedule D-CARE states a 32.5 percent discount applied to the CARE customer's bill prior to the Public Utilities Commission Reimbursement Fee and any applicable user fees, taxes and late payment charges, and this filing does not represent it. The filing carries only the per-line-item components of the same Sheet 1: the Wildfire Fund Non-Bypassable Charge exemption of $0.00591 per kWh, the Fixed Recovery Charge exemption of $0.00619 per kWh, the Base Services Charge Surcharge exemption of $0.064 per meter per day, and the Base Services Charge Discount of $(0.155) per meter per day. Sheet 1 further exempts CARE customers from the CARE Surcharge of $0.208 per meter per day, which no SCE residential rate sheet in this corpus itemizes, so that exemption has no base charge to cancel and is absent. Two percentage benefits on Sheet 6 are also unrepresented: the San Joaquin Valley Disadvantaged Communities Pilot Bill Protection Discount of Special Condition 14 (20 percent in pilot years 1 through 5, then 10 or 20 percent in years 6 through 10) and the 20 percent Transitional Community Solar Discount of Special Condition 15, each limited to pilot participants. Several other Special Conditions are out of scope rather than missing: the income table in Special Condition 2, the application, commencement, verification and change-of-status rules in Special Conditions 4, 5, 7 and 8, and the Arrearage Management Plan debt forgiveness in Special Condition 13 are eligibility and account-administration procedures, not rates. The California Climate Credit of Special Condition 12 is carried on the base rate plans this modifier overlays.
sce:cc-cca-crs-2026-03-20: This filing prices Schedule CCA-CRS for a default CCA or Community Aggregator customer only, and the Applicability and Exemption table on Sheet 3 distinguishes eight customer groups whose component-level exemptions it does not represent. CCA customers on Medical Baseline are exempt from the Wildfire Fund Non-Bypassable Charge; CCA customers on CARE are exempt from both that charge and the Fixed Recovery Charge; CCA customers on FERA are exempt from the Fixed Recovery Charge; Continuous DA/CCA customers are exempt from the Wildfire Fund charge and the Power Charge Indifference Adjustment; Returning Continuous DA customers are exempt from the Wildfire Fund charge. A consumer applying this filing to any of those customers will charge components the tariff exempts. The PCIA Vintage Methodology in Special Condition 1.c is likewise not represented: the filing takes the vintage year as a supplied customer attribute, while the tariff derives it from the Binding Notice of Intent date or the date of initial CCA service, with a vintage determination date before July 1 setting the prior year and one on or after July 1 setting the current year. Special Condition 3, which assigns 2004 vintage to City of Cerritos Community Aggregator customers until that aggregator's annual load reaches 110,000 megawatt-hours, and Special Condition 4, under which a customer switching between DA and CCA service retains the original vintage and exemption status, are also absent. The thirteen non-residential rate groups in the Sheet 4 through Sheet 10 tables are out of scope rather than missing: only the Domestic row belongs in a residential corpus.
sce:cc-da-crs-2026-03-20: This filing prices Schedule DA-CRS for a default Direct Access customer only, and the Applicability and Exemption table on Sheet 3 sets out eight customer groups whose component-level exemptions it does not represent. DA customers on Medical Baseline are exempt from the Wildfire Fund Non-Bypassable Charge; DA customers on CARE are exempt from that charge and from the Fixed Recovery Charge; DA customers on FERA are exempt from the Fixed Recovery Charge; Continuous DA customers are exempt from the Wildfire Fund charge and the Power Charge Indifference Adjustment; Returning Continuous DA customers are exempt from the Wildfire Fund charge. Applying this filing to any of those customers charges components the tariff exempts. The PCIA Vintage Methodology in Special Condition 1.c is not represented either: the filing treats the vintage year as a supplied customer attribute, whereas the tariff fixes Continuous DA customers at the 2001 vintage and derives every other customer's vintage from SCE's acceptance date of the Six-Month Notice to Switch to DA Service, with a determination date before July 1 setting the prior year and one on or after July 1 setting the current year. Special Condition 2, covering Green Rate customers on Schedules GTSR-GR and GTSR-CR whose vintage follows their subscription start date, and Special Condition 3, under which vintage and exemption status survive a switch between DA and CCA service, are also absent. The thirteen non-residential rate groups in the Sheet 4 through Sheet 10 tables are out of scope rather than missing: only the Domestic row belongs in a residential corpus.
sce:cc-fera-2025-11-15: Special Condition 9 of Schedule TOU-D, the Family Electric Rate Assistance Discount, grants an 18.0 percent discount off the customer's bill prior to any applicable taxes and late payment charges, and this filing does not represent it. What is modeled is the rest of Special Condition 9: the Base Services Charge Surcharge exemption of $0.063 per meter per day and the Base Services Charge credit adjustment of $(0.202) per meter per day. Unlike CARE, FERA carries no Wildfire Fund or Fixed Recovery Charge exemption, so those charges apply at the standard rate and their absence here is correct rather than a gap. Because the two modeled adjustments total $(0.265) per meter per day while the unmodeled percentage applies to the whole bill, this filing captures only a small fraction of the FERA benefit for a typical household. The application and eligibility declaration requirement, the rebilling of periods of ineligibility, and the mutual exclusivity with the CARE discount are out of scope rather than missing: they govern enrollment rather than the price of service.
sce:cc-fera-2026-03-20: Special Condition 9 on Sheet 18 of Schedule TOU-D grants FERA households an 18.0 percent discount off their bill prior to any applicable taxes and late payment charges, and this filing does not represent it. The filing carries the two line-item adjustments from the same Special Condition: the Base Services Charge Surcharge exemption of $0.064 per meter per day and the Base Services Charge credit adjustment of $(0.201) per meter per day, together $(0.265) per meter per day. FERA grants no Wildfire Fund Non-Bypassable Charge or Fixed Recovery Charge exemption, so the absence of those credits is faithful rather than a gap. A consumer should read this filing as the small, fixed part of the FERA benefit, with the percentage discount that dominates it left to prose. Note also that the values modeled here are taken from TOU-D Sheet 18 rather than from Schedule D-FERA itself, because Schedule D-FERA Sheet 1 was not reissued when these values were updated and still shows the superseded $0.063 and $(0.202). The enrollment provisions of Special Condition 9, the application and eligibility declaration, the rebilling of ineligible periods, and the exclusion of customers taking the CARE discount, are out of scope rather than missing.
sce:cc-medical-baseline-2025-10-01: Schedule MB-E is a single sheet with a one-sentence Rates section, and it states two effects: the Wildfire Fund Non-Bypassable Charge shall not apply, and the effective Minimum Charge will be $5.00. This filing models the first as a credit of $(0.00591) per kWh cancelling the current base charge, and does not model the second. The $5.00 Minimum Charge is a floor on the bill rather than a per-unit price, and none of the SCE residential base rate plans in this corpus carries a Minimum Charge for it to reduce, the Base Services Charge having replaced the older Basic Charge and Minimum Charge structure. The Applicability sentence, which extends the schedule to all customers receiving a medical baseline allocation, also points at a benefit this filing does not carry: the additional baseline allocation itself, whose kilowatt-hour quantities live in Preliminary Statement Part H rather than on this sheet, and which would have to be expressed as an addition to the base allocation of whichever schedule the customer is on. Note that the modeled credit tracks whatever value the Wildfire Fund charge currently carries; it is stated here at the level effective January 1, 2026, which is later than this schedule's own effective date.
sce:cc-nbt-2025-04-23: This filing carries the per-cell Export Compensation Rates and the structural surface of Schedule NBT, and leaves four priced provisions of the published schedule unrepresented. The Avoided Cost Calculator Plus table in Rates section 3.b lists six Energy Export Credit vintage rows; only the 2025 row is priced here, at $0.024 per kWh for a Residential Non-Equity customer and $0.056 per kWh for a Residential Equity customer, so the 2023 ($0.040 and $0.093), 2024 ($0.032 and $0.074), 2026 ($0.016 and $0.037), 2027 ($0.008 and $0.019) and 2028-and-later (zero) rows are absent. Rates section 4, Net Surplus Compensation, is not modeled: its rate is a rolling twelve-month average of SCE hourly default load aggregation point prices for Hour Ending 08 through Hour Ending 17, recomputed monthly and posted on SCE's website, and it settles against Net Surplus Energy measured over the customer's twelve-month Relevant Period rather than against any one bill. Special Condition 4.e, the Annual True-Up Process, is likewise absent, including the Energy Export Credit Adjustment computed at the then posted Average Retail Export Compensation Rate and the forfeiture of unapplied Energy Export Credits at the end of the Relevant Period. Coverage of the 2026 interconnection vintage is partial: January through May are priced, at 240 Delivery and 240 Generation cells against the 576 and 576 carried for each earlier vintage, because the published hourly export rate data for that vintage did not yet extend past May. The aggregation, paired-storage and multiple-tariff sub-schedules (NBT-A, NBT-PS and NBT-MT) and the NBT-A billing service charges in Rates section 6 (a $25.00 account set-up fee and $20.00 per month for manually billed accounts, $16.00 and $2.70 for automated ones) are out of scope for a residential single-account filing, as are Special Condition 8 on Natural Disaster replacement of a generating facility, Special Condition 9 on Prevailing Wage, and the interconnection and metering requirements in Special Conditions 2 and 3, none of which sets a price.
sce:cc-tou-d-4-9pm-2025-11-15: Two provisions on the Option 4-9 PM rate sheets are not represented in this filing. The first concerns the Baseline Credit of $(0.10449) per kWh: the rate sheet footnote states that the credit applies up to 100 percent of the Baseline Allocation, with additional allocations for customers who have a Heat Pump Water Heater, the allocations themselves being set out in Preliminary Statement Part H. This filing carries the credit as an unbounded per-kilowatt-hour amount with no allocation quantity attached, so a consumer computing a bill from it will credit every kilowatt-hour rather than only those within the customer's baseline, overstating the credit for anyone above baseline. The second is the Option 4-9 PM-CPP variant, whose three prices sit on the same sheet the filing cites: a CPP Event Energy Charge of $0.80000 per kWh, a Summer on-peak non-event energy credit of $(0.15170) per kWh, and a Summer Season Maximum Available Credit of $(0.55677) per kWh for customers grandfathered into dual demand-response participation. None of the three is modeled, so this filing describes the non-CPP option only. Two rate-sheet lines are out of scope rather than missing: the Deed Restricted Base Services Charge discount of $(0.334) per meter per day and the CARE and FERA discount percentages shown at 100.00 are cross-references to separate schedules, each filed as its own modifier overlay in this corpus.

Second, the Option 4-9 PM-CPP variant printed on the same Sheet 2: a CPP Event Energy Charge of $0.80000 per kWh, a Summer on-peak non-event energy credit of $(0.15170) per kWh, and a Summer Season Maximum Available Credit of $(0.58794) per kWh, none of them modeled. Third, the two pilot bill discounts in Special Conditions 15 and 16: the San Joaquin Valley Disadvantaged Communities Pilot Bill Protection Discount (20 percent in years 1 through 5, then 10 or 20 percent in years 6 through 10) and the 20 percent Transitional Community Solar Discount. The Deed Restricted Base Services Charge adjustment of $(0.332) per meter per day and the CARE and FERA discount lines are cross-references to separate schedules, each filed as its own modifier in this corpus.

sce:cc-tou-d-prime-cpp-2026-03-20: This filing carries the three prices Schedule TOU-D publishes for Option PRIME-CPP (a CPP Event Energy Charge of $0.80000 per kWh, a Summer non-event on-peak energy credit of $(0.15170) per kWh, and a Summer Season Maximum Available Credit of $(0.58794) per kWh) and leaves two provisions of Special Condition 4 unrepresented. Special Condition 4.e, Bill Protection, guarantees that a customer on a CPP option is billed no more than they would have been on the corresponding option without CPP for up to the first twelve months of service, delivered as a one-time credit for the positive sum of CPP event charges and summer non-event credits measured over that period. It is not modeled, because it settles across a year of bills rather than within one. Special Condition 4 also states that no CPP credit is provided for exported generation, that is, for energy the customer's generating facility produces and exports during a non-event credit period; this filing's non-event credit applies to the metered quantity without distinguishing import from export, so it will over-credit a customer with behind-the-meter solar. Two further parts of Special Condition 4 are out of scope rather than missing: the event-calling criteria and notification duties in 4.a and 4.c, and the minimum of 12 and maximum of 15 events per calendar year in 4.b, describe how SCE operates the program rather than what a customer is charged. The ineligibility of Direct Access and Community Choice Aggregation customers stated in 4.d is likewise an enrollment restriction rather than a price.
sce:cc-tou-d-prime-2025-11-15: Two conditional credits on the Option PRIME rate sheet are carried here without the conditions that gate them. The sheet labels them EV Meter Credit (Separately Metered EV Option) at $(0.446) per meter per day and EV Submeter Credit at $(0.152) per meter per day; this filing states both as unconditional price definitions, so a consumer computing a bill from it will apply both to every Option PRIME customer rather than only to one with an SCE-provided separate electric vehicle meter or a qualifying submeter. The Option PRIME-CPP variant on the same sheet is also unrepresented at this effective date: its CPP Event Energy Charge of $0.80000 per kWh, Summer on-peak non-event energy credit of $(0.15170) per kWh, and Summer Season Maximum Available Credit of $(0.55677) per kWh are not modeled here and no companion filing carries them for 2025-11-15. Option PRIME has no Baseline Credit line, so the baseline-allocation limitation that affects the other SCE residential options does not arise. Three rate-sheet lines are out of scope rather than missing: the Deed Restricted Base Services Charge discount of $(0.334) per meter per day, the CARE and FERA discount percentages shown at 100.00, and the Medical Line Item Discount shown at 100.000 are cross-references to separate schedules, each filed as its own modifier overlay in this corpus.
sce:cc-tou-d-prime-2026-03-20: Two conditional credits on Sheet 6 are carried here without the conditions that gate them. The sheet labels them EV Meter Credit (Separately Metered EV Option) at $(0.451) per meter per day and EV Submeter Credit at $(0.152) per meter per day, and Special Conditions 6 and 19 restrict them to a customer with a separate SCE-provided electric vehicle meter and to a customer using a submeter meeting the Plug-In Electric Vehicle Submetering Protocol respectively. This filing states both as unconditional price definitions, so a consumer computing a bill will apply both to every Option PRIME customer. The two pilot bill discounts in Special Conditions 15 and 16 are also unrepresented: the San Joaquin Valley Disadvantaged Communities Pilot Bill Protection Discount (20 percent in years 1 through 5, then 10 or 20 percent in years 6 through 10) and the 20 percent Transitional Community Solar Discount. Option PRIME has no Baseline Credit line, so the baseline-allocation limitation affecting the other SCE residential options does not arise here. Several things are out of scope rather than missing: the Option PRIME-CPP prices printed on the same sheet are filed as a companion modifier overlay in this corpus rather than here; the Deed Restricted Base Services Charge adjustment of $(0.332) per meter per day, the CARE and FERA discount lines, and the Medical Baseline Credit line shown at 100.00 are cross-references to separate schedules each filed on its own; and the attestation-based eligibility of Special Condition 5, the twelve-month rate change restriction of Special Condition 7 and the Arrearage Management Plan of Special Condition 10 govern enrollment and account administration rather than price.
